sample_design: Eight previously unaudited identities across seven manufacturers, fixed before classification against merged post-PR #62 main. The cohort intentionally moves away from the AnchorAttachment region stressed by V3/V4: it contains four ToolAttachments and four tethers, no AnchorAttachment products, no wrist/bucket-lip cases, and no V1-V4 or PR #58/#60/#61/#62 proof identity. It mixes existing-adapter manufacturers with manufacturers that still require catalogue onboarding so the audit can distinguish core semantic portability from ingestion throughput.
audit_question: Against merged post-PR #62 main, does a materially different fresh ToolAttachment/tether cohort now land predominantly in A/B without a comparable recurring C/D seam, such that portability can become a periodic stress test while development shifts toward catalogue throughput and the demand-side MVP?
decision: Do not shift the development centre fully to catalogue throughput yet. V5 is strongly A/B-majority by count and D remains zero, but the two independent C cases expose the same narrow reusable compiler seam: source-backed dimensional fit constraints cannot yet be composed onto an arbitrary concrete ToolInterfaceFeature eligibility path. Runtime FeaturePredicate already supports feature-local dimensions, while claim resolution currently compiles numeric fit only for external_section_attachment with a complete min/max diameter envelope and deliberately leaves handle_attachment dimension-free. Close only that generic feature-bound dimensional eligibility seam, preserving same-feature binding and fail-closed evidence scope; do not add battery-, screwdriver-, FallTech- or Ergodyne-specific compatibility rules. Treat the six B cases as catalogue-throughput evidence. After the dimensional seam is vertically proven, run another materially different fresh portability sample; if it has no comparable recurring C/D pressure, portability should become a periodic stress test and development should pivot to catalogue throughput plus the demand-side MVP.

products.name: Battery Boot Tool Attachment
observed_public_facts: adjustable hook-and-loop straps retain the attachment around cordless power-tool batteries
published fit scope is batteries up to 3.5 in long x 2.75 in wide x 2.5 in high
steel D-ring provides the tether connection point
6 lb maximum battery/tool load
core_fit: one concrete tool/configuration feature can already carry arbitrary feature-local dimensions
runtime EligibilityPath and FeaturePredicate can already evaluate multiple dimensions against the same bound feature
required_core_changes: generalize attachment-eligibility claim composition so accepted source-backed dimensional upper/lower bounds can be compiled onto one selected ToolInterfaceFeature path instead of only the existing external-section min/max-diameter special case

represent the installed battery body as one resolved external geometry feature only when demand-side tool/configuration evidence establishes that feature; do not add a battery-SKU compatibility branch
products.portability_gap: The model can store the boot, D-ring and load rating, and its runtime predicate layer is already dimension-generic. The production resolver cannot faithfully enforce the manufacturer's three-axis fit envelope: external_section_attachment is hard-wired to a complete min/max diameter pair, while ignoring the published L/W/H limits would over-authorize installation. This is therefore a reusable feature-bound dimensional-eligibility gap rather than a FallTech exception.

products.name: Tool Grip and Tether Attachment Point - 2-Pack
observed_public_facts: two-piece rubber sleeve and end cap encapsulate screwdriver or nut-driver handles
published compatibility is handle diameter 1.0 to 1.28 in with handle height 4.5 in
swiveling end cap provides the tether connection point
1 lb maximum working capacity and 48 in maximum tether length
core_fit: mechanical-capture style retention and ToolAttachment-provided tether interface
required_core_changes: extend the same generic feature-bound dimensional eligibility composition so handle_attachment can retain and enforce explicit accepted handle-diameter and handle-height fit evidence on the exact selected handle rather than remaining geometry-only
products.portability_gap: The current handle_attachment compiler intentionally emits only feature_kind = handle and carries no inferred dimensional fit. That was correct for SnapLock/Quick Spin evidence, but it cannot faithfully ingest an attachment whose manufacturer publishes an explicit numeric handle envelope. Dropping the 1.0-1.28 in diameter and 4.5 in height conditions would broaden eligibility beyond the source. This independently repeats FallTech 5401A1's compiler-level dimensional-binding gap.

products.name: 35 lb Medium Duty Cinch Tool Attachment (No Tabs)
observed_public_facts: pass-through loop provides cinch installation on tools
web loop provides the tether-side connection
35 lb maximum load
manufacturer instructions separately identify difficult-to-tether examples including closed-handle tools and prohibit use on tapered handles
core_fit: existing captive-handle eligibility can represent the explicit closed-handle subset without treating illustrative tool categories as a closed whitelist
existing prohibited_surface_profile constraint can preserve the tapered-handle prohibition
ToolAttachment-provided loop interface and rated capacity
products.portability_gap: Safewaze ToolAttachment acquisition/extraction is missing. The public evidence should be compiled conservatively: the broad 'wide variety of tools' wording and illustrative clamps/wrenches are not themselves a new generic eligibility rule, while the existing cinch, closed-handle subset, surface-profile prohibition, loop interface and capacity primitives already carry the executable facts that are established.

products.name: Tool Catch 25mm x 90mm - 5 Pack
observed_public_facts: Tool Catch is secured to the tool using GRIPPS V-Gripp Tape
installation instructs repeated tight tape wraps while leaving the ring uncovered
ring provides the load-rated tether connection point
2.5 kg / 5.5 lb maximum load
products.portability_gap: The existing GRIPPS ToolAttachment extractor is SnapLock-focused, so Tool Catch plus V-Gripp Tape needs catalogue extraction and evidence-bound required pairing. The neutral wrap/required-pairing/assembly/interface/capacity model already exists; no Tool Catch-specific recommendation primitive is required.

products.name: 15lb Locking Tool Lanyard
observed_public_facts: 3 ft lanyard with 15 lb weight rating
locking carabiners require double actions to open
an integrated swiveling carabiner reduces twisting
shock-absorbing lanyard body is described as slowing a dropped tool gradually
core_fit: carabiner ConnectorSpec with opening-action and swivel attributes
working-length facts where source-local endpoint evidence supports them
shock-absorbing construction may remain descriptive evidence unless a later rule consumes it
products.portability_gap: The current Milwaukee adapter is not a general tether catalogue extractor. Onboarding this lanyard requires product-local endpoint/topology extraction and source scoping, but the published locking, swivel, length and load facts fit existing neutral tether and connector primitives.

products.name: Bungee Tether Single-Action - 2.5kg / 5.5lb
observed_public_facts: elasticised polyester bungee construction
wide tail loop with grip weave can fasten to tools or anchor points
product description calls the carabiner dual-action while the product title says Single-Action
2.5 kg / 5.5 lb maximum load
evidence_notes: The title/description action-count inconsistency is an evidence-reconciliation issue. Do not normalize an opening-action count until product-local evidence resolves it; it is not a reason to invent a new connector primitive.
core_fit: loop engagement and endpoint role can remain evidence-bound/reversible where the manufacturer permits either tool or anchor use
elastic tether construction and rated capacity
products.portability_gap: GRIPPS tether extraction is currently optimized for explicit dedicated anchor/tool dual-carabiner wording. H01072 needs broader vendor extraction plus conservative reconciliation of the action-count conflict, not a new downstream topology or compatibility rule.

products.name: DBI-SALA Hook2Loop Bungee Tool Tether
observed_public_facts: one self-locking carabiner end and one loop end
manufacturer instructions allow either end to attach to the tool and the other to an off-body/fixed anchor point
loop end is cinched by feeding the carabiner end through the loop
15 lb load rating with published relaxed/stretched working lengths
core_fit: minimum/retracted and maximum/extended length facts and rated capacity
products.portability_gap: The 3M adapter is intentionally Quick Spin ToolAttachment-specific. Hook2Loop needs tether acquisition/extraction and identity-scoped document joining, but its reversible carabiner/loop topology, cinch mechanism, length and capacity are already represented by existing neutral primitives.

products.name: Arc Flash Tool Tether
observed_public_facts: steel screw-gate carabiner endpoint
Kevlar cord loop endpoint
27 in tether length
manufacturer states ASTM F887 arc-flash compliance and Kevlar/Nomex heat- and burn-resistant webbing
evidence_notes: Arc-flash compliance is a positive capability claim, not an explicit prohibition on ordinary tether use. V5 therefore does not create a hard environmental rule from the marketing/certification label alone. If future demand-side scenarios repeatedly require positive arc-flash suitability to decide among otherwise viable candidates, that should be audited as a separate evidence-backed environmental expansion.
core_fit: standards/compliance evidence retained without converting positive certification into an unsupported hard compatibility rule
products.portability_gap: Guardian catalogue acquisition remains missing. The tether can participate through existing endpoint, connector, length and evidence primitives. Its arc-flash certification should be preserved as evidence, but absence of a current positive environmental preference primitive does not prevent baseline recommendation participation and is not promoted to C from one sampled product.
